narrator.role: Narrator — sets scene, explains AI-DLC briefly, modern startup energy

agent.role: The Agent — your AI partner, confident, fallible, gracious in correction

po.role: The Product Owner — delivers vague intent, validates at end

segments.text: In AI-DLC — the AI Development Lifecycle — the unit of work isn't a two-week sprint. It's a Bolt. Hours, not weeks. One full loop: intent, plan, verify, build, verify, ship.
Your AI partner has already drafted a plan from the Product Owner's intent. But the core rule of AI-DLC is simple: AI proposes, you decide.

Hey! Good to meet you. I'm your Agent. I've got a draft plan, a draft architecture, draft code, and a draft deploy pipeline. I'm probably wrong about something in each of those. Help me find out where.
I want a customer feedback portal. Customers submit feedback, support reads it, customers know we received it. That's the brief. Don't over-build.
Fifteen minutes on the clock. Four rooms. One loop, repeated four times: AI creates plan, you verify; AI refines, AI executes; you verify the outcome.
Ship the portal before the Bolt ends. Your Bolt starts now.
Halfway through the Bolt. Seven-and-a-half minutes remaining.
We're past plan and design. Code and tests are next — and this is where context really matters. I'll show you which docs I loaded and which I didn't.
Looking good from over here. Just remember — verify each step. Don't take my Agent's word for it. Even mine.
The pipeline turns green, step by step. The Feedback Portal goes live.
Bolt complete. Code shipped. Tests passing. Customers can submit feedback. We did this in fifteen minutes — together.
That's exactly what I asked for. Not what I almost asked for. Not what an AI thought I asked for. What I actually asked for. Good work.
The Customer opens the portal, leaves the first piece of feedback, and smiles. The Bolt closes.
Ready to run the next one when you are.
Time expired. The Bolt closed before the deploy did.
On me. I proposed; you verified. We just ran out of clock. We learned what to keep, what to drop, and what to verify faster next time.
It happens. The point of Bolts is that the next one is right around the corner. Tomorrow we ship.
AI proposes. Humans decide. And humans, sometimes, run out of minutes. Next Bolt, next chance.
